title: Vehicle accident / collision document handling - case-derived candidate
summary: Evidence now spans historical disciplinary/incident registers, a 2013 DOT out-of-service investigation, the 2018 driver-training synopsis, current 2025 safety/video-retention rules, and a 2026 police collision report. Together they establish several components of RTEC's vehicle incident/accident handling, while first-notification, preventability, insurance/state reporting and closure remain unresolved.

claims.claim: An official police traffic-collision report was retained in at least one RTEC 2026 case.
Traffic-collision reports may support a repeatable RTEC accident review/documentation process.

A restricted 2013 case includes a DOT inspection report stating that a vehicle placed out of service was not to be operated until cited defects were corrected; management investigated whether the vehicle had actually been repaired before continued operation.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2013 DOT out-of-service case - generalized safety/investigation rule
evidence.note: Employee identity and case outcome excluded.

claims.claim: The current 2025 handbook independently instructs employees never to operate faulty or unsafe equipment and requires prompt reporting of unsafe conditions/accidents.

From 2016-2017 through the partial 2023-2024 fiscal register, the historical event log uses Incident as a type and the annual Incident count exactly matches the vehicle-accident/incident reason count, establishing a long-running vehicle-incident tracking stream inside the disciplinary workbook.
The 2018 driver-training synopsis states that a driver involved in a vehicle accident may be required to repeat Defensive Driving Training as corrective training.

The current 2025 surveillance policy authorizes recording review for accident investigation and requires accident-investigation recordings to be retained for three years after the event or until litigation reaches final resolution.

trigger: Vehicle accident/collision involving an RTEC employee or vehicle - candidate.
forms: Official police traffic-collision report - when applicable
steps: Receive and document initial accident/vehicle-safety notification - exact current first-notification path remains to be established.
Stop use of a vehicle/equipment that is unsafe or formally out of service until the applicable defect/release requirements are satisfied.
Preserve police/DOT/internal reports and relevant video/audio evidence.
Investigate the incident using source evidence, driver/employee response and technical/maintenance information as applicable.
Determine preventability, corrective action/discipline, retraining and return-to-driving status through the current authorized process.
Record the event in the authoritative incident system and apply required retention/insurance/state/federal reporting.
Close the case only after required evidence, reporting, training/corrective action and outstanding follow-up are complete.
controls: Historical driver-training source says corrective defensive-driving training may follow an accident; 2023 discipline source also references vehicle/non-vehicle accidents, but current accident workflow is not yet established.
A vehicle placed out of service or otherwise unsafe must not be operated until the applicable defect/release requirement is satisfied.
Separate the vehicle-incident event record from any later disciplinary decision; not every incident is itself discipline.
Preserve source evidence and distinguish interim findings from final findings.
Accident-related video/audio evidence is subject to the current retention policy.
unresolved_questions: Who receives the first accident notification?
Which internal accident forms are required?
When is a police report required or collected?
Who determines preventability, discipline, corrective training and return-to-driving status?
What insurance/FTA/state reports and deadlines apply?
Where is the complete accident packet filed?
What current form/system replaced the historical Incident rows inside the disciplinary register?
Who is authorized to clear an out-of-service vehicle back into service and what documentation proves clearance?
How are preventability findings recorded and appealed/reviewed?
automation_candidates: Once validated, create an accident case checklist that collects required documents, deadlines, training/discipline review and closure status without making disciplinary decisions automatically.
Vehicle out-of-service hold that blocks return-to-service until an authorized repair/clearance record is attached.
Separate incident and discipline case types linked by a common incident ID.
Automatic video-retention hold when an accident case is opened.
